questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university and the city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the social aspect and the city was really nice, but I was surprised at how low the academic level was

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was very easy - the intro days at uni were good

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: intro days and helt from the secretarial office

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a list on the university web-page and just wrote to the company through their website - very easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it worked well - I lived with seven other students, so it was a good way of making friends. the only thing is that the possibility of getting your deposit back is rather low. but overall a good experience. but I know that I was lucky and found a good place - som people were scammed and payed twice as much for very bad facilities, so be sure to check trustpilot etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: for me, it was very easy, I just got the courses that I first picked. I know for others, this was a long, hard process because they didn't get the approved and so on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the secretarial office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: they were fine

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just be sure to pick courses that you know will get accepted

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: unfortunately, it was a very low academic level

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was shockingly low... most of my courses were master courses and as I am I BA student I was a little worried upon arrival, about wether it would be too difficult. this was not the case - the best course I had, was a course where they had a guest professor from university of cambridge

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: i liked that the hos university had much smaller classes so most of my lectures were In classrooms, which facilitated much more dialogue

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. field research 
2. contemporary social inequalities 
3. Portuguese history and culture 
4. Archival research and other sources 
5. inquiry methods online

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the Portuguese history and culture course and the contemporary social inequalities (because of the guest professor)

questions.answer: visit Nazare, sintra, cascais and porto. go surfing and hiking

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy. the Portuguese people are very sweet and open

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the Portuguese people are very laidback, which most of the time was very nice but they were often late etc

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: their openness and kindness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. don't expect much on an academic level - do it for the social experience and two grow as a person 
2. people are very sweet and helpfull 
3. they have attendance, so it mandatory to attend 80% of all classes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: growing as a person and meeting people form all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: creating a new life in a new city
